vignette:
Mark, a 50-year-old psychologist, sits in his office, the familiar scent of old books and freshly brewed coffee surrounding him. The soft hum of the air-conditioning unit is a constant, yet today it feels like an unwelcome reminder of the world outside, a world he often struggles to engage with. He glances at the clock on the wall, noting the time. His next client is due any minute, but he finds himself lost in thought, the shadows of his past creeping into the bright space he has created for his practice.

It has been two years since the traumatic event, yet the memory remains vivid. Mark recalls that night with unsettling clarity. He had been attending a conference, a gathering of like-minded professionals discussing the nuances of trauma therapy. He had felt invigorated by the conversations and connections he made. After an evening of networking, he found himself walking back to his hotel, the streetlights casting long shadows on the pavement. The air was cool, and he felt a sense of safety in the bustling city, until it wasn't safe anymore.

He remembers the sudden grip on his arm, the fear that surged through him like ice water. The struggle was brief, a blur of violence and violation that left him feeling both powerless and ashamed. The incident shattered him. Mark had spent the following weeks in a haze, oscillating between disbelief and anger. He had been trained to help others navigate their trauma, yet he found himself paralyzed by his own.

Returning to his practice was not easy. His clients, often dealing with their own painful histories, became mirrors reflecting his internal turmoil. He notices how he has begun to withdraw, to create barriers between himself and those who seek his guidance. The empathy that once flowed freely has become a trickle. He feels as if he is floating through their sessions, the words of his clients muffled and distant. Each time he hears a story of trauma, he feels the walls of his own experience closing in, and he struggles to breathe.

In the months following the incident, Mark's life became a series of carefully constructed routines designed to keep the chaos at bay. He wakes up early, sometimes before dawn, to exercise, a futile attempt to outrun the shadows of his mind. He is meticulous in his work, pouring over notes and research, trying to immerse himself in the lives of others instead of confronting his own. Yet, when he closes the door to his office at the end of the day, he often finds the quiet unbearable. It is in those still moments that the memories invade-images of that night, the feeling of helplessness, and the shame that clings to him like a second skin.

Mark's marriage has also felt the strain. His wife, Linda, is a compassionate woman, always reaching for him, trying to bridge the gap that has formed between them. He sees the concern in her eyes, the way she hesitates before asking him about his day. He wants to tell her everything, to share the burdens he carries, but the words stick in his throat. Instead, he offers her the façade of normalcy, a smile that doesn't quite reach his eyes. They often sit in silence, the weight of unsaid things hanging between them.

During our sessions together, Mark speaks in fragments. He shares his dreams, dark and chaotic, where he relives that night over and over, the sense of dread waking him in the early hours. He talks about his practice, the clients he feels he is failing, and the guilt that gnaws at him when he feels incapable of providing the support they need. He grapples with the notion of vulnerability, recognizing that his own experiences have made him more attuned to the suffering of others, yet he fears that opening up will shatter the carefully curated image he has constructed as a healer.

As he navigates this tumultuous landscape, Mark grapples with feelings of isolation. He seeks solace in the few friendships he maintains, but even those connections feel strained. He often finds himself withdrawing, retreating into the safe confines of his home where he can control the noise of the outside world. In these moments, he finds himself reflecting on the irony of his profession; he is a psychologist haunted by the very traumas he helps others to overcome. 

Mark's journey is a complex tapestry of healing, resilience, and the ongoing struggle to reclaim his sense of self. Each session peels back layers of pain, revealing both the fragility and strength that coexist within him, as he learns to navigate the intricate dance between his past and present.
